newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes firmer on fund inflows.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes firmer on fund inflows.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar finished slightly higher against its U.S. counterpart on Saturday despite an unexpected rate cut by the central bank on Friday.
Dealers attributed the local unit's rise to huge inflows of foreign equity funds.
"The Taiwan dollar would have fallen to reflect the cut in banks' reserve requirements, but the huge foreign fund inflows eased the depreciation pressure," said one dealers.
The local unit ended at T$27.476 against Saturday's T$27.488 close. Turnover was an active US$133 million in the shortened Saturday session.
Dealers expected the Taiwan dollar to fall next week.
"Recent economic indicators show Taiwan's economy is still gloomy, I think the local currency will test its lower level next week," the dealer said.
Taiwan's statistics bureau forecast that gross domestic product growth for the entire year would reach 5.89 percent, well below an earlier prediction of 6.17 percent.
A range of T$27.46-53 was seen.
